props.title: The World According to Monsanto

sections.content: The World According to Monsanto stands as a pivotal documentary exposing corporate control of agriculture, joining other hard-hitting food industry investigations like Food, Inc. (2008) and King Corn (2007). French filmmaker Marie-Monique Robin meticulously traces Monsanto's evolution from chemical company to biotech giant, using damning internal documents and whistleblower interviews. The film's methodical approach influenced later corporate exposés like The Corporation (2003) and Inside Job (2010), establishing a template for investigating powerful multinationals through rigorous research and compelling personal stories.

sections.content: The film sparked a wave of agricultural documentaries that expanded beyond single-company investigations to examine systemic issues. Fresh (2009) offered solutions through sustainable farming alternatives, while GMO OMG (2013) explored the personal stakes for families trying to avoid genetically modified foods. These films share Robin's investigative rigor but add constructive approaches to food system reform. SUBHEAD: Impact on Environmental Documentary Filmmaking

Robin's technique of combining corporate paper trails with human impact stories influenced major environmental documentaries like The Cove (2009) and Gasland (2010). Her approach of methodically building evidence while maintaining narrative tension became a blueprint for investigative environmental films. Cowspiracy (2014) and Seaspiracy (2021) notably adopted similar strategies of following paper trails to expose industry cover-ups.
